        "diffString": "- \n+ \"\"\"\n+ Blender version helpers for BasedPlayblast.\n+ \n+ Keeps the add-on logic clean by centralizing all version comparisons and\n+ common constants for the supported tracks (4.4 LTS, 4.5 LTS, 5.0+).\n+ \"\"\"\n+ \n+ from __future__ import annotations\n+ \n+ try:  # Blender runtime\n+     import bpy  # type: ignore\n+ except ImportError:  # During static analysis or packaging\n+     bpy = None  # type: ignore\n+ \n+ # Targeted LTS anchors\n+ VERSION_4_4_LTS = (4, 4, 0)\n+ VERSION_4_5_LTS = (4, 5, 0)\n+ VERSION_5_0 = (5, 0, 0)\n+ \n+ \n+ def _current_version() -&gt; tuple[int, int, int]:\n+     \"\"\"Return Blender's version tuple or a fallback.\"\"\"\n+     if bpy and getattr(bpy.app, \"version\", None):\n+         return bpy.app.version  # type: ignore[return-value]\n+     return (0, 0, 0)\n+ \n+ \n+ def get_blender_version() -&gt; tuple[int, int, int]:\n+     return _current_version()\n+ \n+ \n+ def get_version_string() -&gt; str:\n+     v = _current_version()\n+     return f\"{v[0]}.{v[1]}.{v[2]}\"\n+ \n+ \n+ def is_version_at_least(major: int, minor: int = 0, patch: int = 0) -&gt; bool:\n+     current = _current_version()\n+     return current &gt;= (major, minor, patch)\n+ \n+ \n+ def is_version_less_than(major: int, minor: int = 0, patch: int = 0) -&gt; bool:\n+     current = _current_version()\n+     return current &lt; (major, minor, patch)\n+ \n+ \n+ def get_version_category() -&gt; str:\n+     \"\"\"\n+     Collapse Blender versions into the compatibility buckets we actively test.\n+     \"\"\"\n+     major, minor, _ = _current_version()\n+     if major &lt; 4:\n+         return f\"{major}.{minor}\"\n+     if major == 4 and minor &lt; 5:\n+         return \"4.4\"\n+     if major == 4:\n+         return \"4.5\"\n+     return \"5.0+\"\n+ \n+ \n+ def is_supported() -&gt; bool:\n+     \"\"\"Check if the detected version is at least our minimum target.\"\"\"\n+     return not is_version_less_than(*VERSION_4_4_LTS)\n+ ",

  "contentsAfterEdit": "\"\"\"\r\nBlender version helpers for BasedPlayblast.\r\n\r\nKeeps the add-on logic clean by centralizing all version comparisons and\r\ncommon constants for the supported tracks (4.4 LTS, 4.5 LTS, 5.0+).\r\n\"\"\"\r\n\r\nfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\ntry:  # Blender runtime\r\n    import bpy  # type: ignore\r\nexcept ImportError:  # During static analysis or packaging\r\n    bpy = None  # type: ignore\r\n\r\n# Targeted LTS anchors\r\nVERSION_4_4_LTS = (4, 4, 0)\r\nVERSION_4_5_LTS = (4, 5, 0)\r\nVERSION_5_0 = (5, 0, 0)\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _current_version() -&gt; tuple[int, int, int]:\r\n    \"\"\"Return Blender's version tuple or a fallback.\"\"\"\r\n    if bpy and getattr(bpy.app, \"version\", None):\r\n        return bpy.app.version  # type: ignore[return-value]\r\n    return (0, 0, 0)\r\n\r\n\r\ndef get_blender_version() -&gt; tuple[int, int, int]:\r\n    return _current_version()\r\n\r\n\r\ndef get_version_string() -&gt; str:\r\n    v = _current_version()\r\n    return f\"{v[0]}.{v[1]}.{v[2]}\"\r\n\r\n\r\ndef is_version_at_least(major: int, minor: int = 0, patch: int = 0) -&gt; bool:\r\n    current = _current_version()\r\n    return current &gt;= (major, minor, patch)\r\n\r\n\r\ndef is_version_less_than(major: int, minor: int = 0, patch: int = 0) -&gt; bool:\r\n    current = _current_version()\r\n    return current &lt; (major, minor, patch)\r\n\r\n\r\ndef get_version_category() -&gt; str:\r\n    \"\"\"\r\n    Collapse Blender versions into the compatibility buckets we actively test.\r\n    \"\"\"\r\n    major, minor, _ = _current_version()\r\n    if major &lt; 4:\r\n        return f\"{major}.{minor}\"\r\n    if major == 4 and minor &lt; 5:\r\n        return \"4.4\"\r\n    if major == 4:\r\n        return \"4.5\"\r\n    return \"5.0+\"\r\n\r\n\r\ndef is_supported() -&gt; bool:\r\n    \"\"\"Check if the detected version is at least our minimum target.\"\"\"\r\n    return not is_version_less_than(*VERSION_4_4_LTS)\r\n\r\n"

icon_only=True, emboss=False)\r\n        row.label(text=\"Properties\")\r\n        row.operator(\"bpl.apply_user_defaults\", text=\"\", icon='PREFERENCES')\r\n        \r\n        if show_props:\r\n Display Mode\r\n            display_box = props_box.box()\r\n            display_box.label(text=\"Display Mode\", icon='SHADING_RENDERED')\r\n            col = display_box.column(align=True)\r\n            col.prop(props, \"display_mode\", text=\"\")\r\n            col.prop(props, \"auto_disable_overlays\")\r\n            col.prop(props, \"enable_depth_of_field\")\r\n            \r\n            # 2. Metadata\r\n            metadata_box = props_box.box()\r\n            metadata_box.label(text=\"Metadata\", icon='TEXT')\r\n            col = metadata_box.column(align=True)\r\n            col.prop(props, \"show_metadata\", text=\"Show Metadata\")\r\n            \r\n            if props.show_metadata:\r\n                col.prop(props, \"metadata_note\", text=\"\")\r\n                \r\n                row = col.row(align=True)\r\n                row.prop(props, \"metadata_date\", toggle=True)\r\n                row.prop(props, \"metadata_frame\", toggle=True)\r\n                row.prop(props, \"metadata_scene\", toggle=True)\r\n                \r\n                row = col.row(align=True)\r\n                row.prop(props, \"metadata_camera\", toggle=True)\r\n                row.prop(props, \"metadata_lens\", toggle=True)\r\n                row.prop(props, \"metadata_resolution\", toggle=True)\r\n\r\n# Define the addon preferences class\r\nclass BPL_AddonPreferences(AddonPreferences):\r\n    bl_idname = __name__\r\n    \r\n    default_video_quality: EnumProperty(\r\n        name=\"Default Video Quality\",\r\n        description=\"Default quality setting for the add-on. ## Updates
- Added reusable version + compatibility modules so we no longer scatter `bpy.app.version` checks across the add-on; helpers now centralize version buckets (4.4 LTS, 4.5 LTS, 5.0+) and rendering shims such as safe OpenGL invocation and studio-light resolution.
```1:58:utils/version.py
"""
Blender version helpers for BasedPlayblast.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

try:
    import bpy  # type: ignore
except ImportError:
    bpy = None  # type: ignore

VERSION_4_4_LTS = (4, 4, 0)
VERSION_4_5_LTS = (4, 5, 0)
VERSION_5_0 = (5, 0, 0)

def get_blender_version() -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    if bpy and getattr(bpy.app, "version", None):
        return bpy.app.version  # type: ignore[return-value]
    return (0, 0, 0)

def get_version_category() -> str:
    major, minor, _ = get_blender_version()
    if major == 4 and minor < 5:
        return "4.4"
    if major == 4:
        return "4.5"
    return "5.0+"
```
- Refactored the main operator to use the compat helpers for video-format selection, viewport OpenGL rendering, and HDRI discovery, so Blender 4.4/4.5/5.0 paths all flow through the same code.
```440:907:__init__.py

Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            #   "contentsAfterEdit": "# BasedPlayblast\n\n**Easily create playblasts from Blender**\n\nBasedPlayblast is a Blender addon that streamlines the process of creating video playblasts for animation review. It provides optimized render settings for fast preview generation while maintaining visual quality suitable for review purposes.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Fast Playblast Creation**: Optimized render settings for different preview modes (Solid, Material, Rendered)\n- **Multiple Display Modes**: Support for Wireframe, Solid, Material Preview, and Rendered modes\n- **Flexible Resolution**: Scene, preset, or custom resolution options\n- **Video Format Support**: MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV with various codecs (H.264, H.265, AV1, etc.)\n- **Metadata Integration**: Automatic inclusion of frame numbers, camera info, and custom notes\n- **Settings Management**: Apply and restore render settings without losing your project configuration\n- **Flamenco Support**: Custom Flamenco Job Script with a simple, non-destructive workflow\n\n## Installation\n\n### Via BlenderKit's Extension Repository (Recommended)\n1. Open Blender (4.2 LTS or newer)\n2. Install BlenderKit via https://www.blenderkit.com/get-blenderkit/\n3. Open Preferences (Ctrl + ,)\n4. Go to **Edit &gt; Preferences &gt; Get Extensions**\n5. Search for \"BasedPlayblast\"\n6. Click **Install**\n7. Enjoy automatic updating!\n\n### Manual Installation\n1. Download the latest release, or the release that supports your intended Blender version\n2. In Blender, go to **Edit &gt; Preferences &gt; Add-ons**\n3. Click **Install from Disk** and select the downloaded file\n4. Enable the addon in the list\n\n## Usage\n\n1. **Locate the Panel**: Go to **Properties &gt; Output &gt; BasedPlayblast**\n2. **Configure Settings**: Set your output path, resolution, and display mode\n3. **Create Playblast**: Click the **PLAYBLAST** button\n4. **View Result**: Click **VIEW** to open the generated video\n\n- **Apply Blast Settings**: Use this button to apply optimized render settings without rendering\n    - Intended particularly for Flamenco. Apply, check the resultant render settings to ensure they're correct, then send to Flamenco using the BasedPlayblast custom Job type.\n- **Restore Original Settings**: Return to your original render configuration\n- **Display Modes**:\n    - **Wireframe/Solid**\n        - Fast workbench viewport rendering. Recommended for short and/or locally-blasted projects.\n    - **Material**\n    - **Rendered**\n\n## Requirements\n\n- Blender 4.2 LTS or newer (validated on 4.2 LTS, 4.5 LTS, and 5.0+)\n- Python 3.x (included with Blender)\n\n## Support\n\n- **Documentation**: [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/RaincloudTheDragon/BasedPlayblast)\n- **Issues**: Report bugs or request features on GitHub\n- **License**: GPL-3.0-or-later"

We’d need to push a new extension build with `blender_version_min = "4.2.0"` (and make sure the BlenderKit entry uses that build) before the marketplace install will work on 4.2.

We should tweak `compat.viewport_opengl_render` so that when it’s handed a RegionView3D (like `self._region_3d`), it ignores that and still grabs the associated WINDOW region from the area. That way the override always passes a real `bpy.types.Region`, and the OpenGL render won’t throw that error. Let me know if you want me to patch that next.

**Analyzing completion detection bug**

I'm reviewing logs and the issue showing completion detection stalls unless the playhead hits an outer frame. I see that progress hangs until manual intervention, then completion triggers after frame 51 despite the file being incomplete. I want to suggest adjusting detection logic to rely on counts rather than the current frame and consider proposing a fix along with next steps.</details></think>

---

I saw the same behavior in your 4.2 session: OpenGL render finishes all 50 frames, but `Detected playblast completion - frames complete: True, files complete: False` only fires after you touch the timeline (frame jumps from 48 → 51). That lines up exactly with issue #5, where completion depends on the playhead hitting the out point [^1].

Root cause is in `BPL_OT_playblast_modal`: the loop marks completion when either
- `self._max_frame_seen >= self._frame_end`, or
- expected files exist on disk.

`self._max_frame_seen` only advances when `frame_current` changes, so if Blender’s viewport stops updating at frame 48 the operator never sees frame 50 unless you jog the playhead manually. We need to decouple completion from `frame_current` and instead track rendered frame counts or file creation directly.

Next steps I can take:
1. Adjust the modal loop to poll for output files (PNG or video) and use file counts/timestamps as the primary completion metric.
2. Optionally add a watchdog to force‐query the dependency graph for `frame_current` once the render operator reports “FINISHED”.

Let me know if you want me to move ahead on that fix; otherwise I can keep digging into why the viewport stops at frame 48 in some OpenGL renders.

[^1]: [Playhead must be moved to the out point in order for the blast to finalize #5](https://github.com/RaincloudTheDragon/BasedPlayblast/issues/5)

View Playblast Operator\nclass BPL_OT_view_playblast(Operator):\n    bl_idname = \"bpl.view_playblast\"\n    bl_label = \"View Playblast\"\n    bl_description = \"Play back rendered Playblast\"\n    bl_options = {'REGISTER', 'UNDO'}\n    \n    def execute(self, context):\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        # Check if we have a playblast file\n {os.path.basename(filepath)}\")\n        \n        # Open the file with the default system application\n        try:\n            if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                os.startfile(filepath)\n            elif sys.platform == 'darwin':  # macOS\n                subprocess.call(('open', filepath))\n            else:  # Linux and other Unix-like\n                subprocess.call(('xdg-open', Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # Pattern 3: Files with .mp4 in name (Blender 5.0 issue - wrong extension in path)\n            frame_pattern3 = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \".mp4%04d.png\")\n            \n            # Try to find which pattern matches actual files\n            import glob\n            test_patterns = [\n                (frame_pattern1, output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern2, frame_output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern3, output_dir)\n            ]\n            \n            frame_pattern = None\n            frame_dir = None\n            for pattern, dir_path in test_patterns:\n                # Test if files matching this pattern exist\n                test_files = glob.glob(pattern.replace(\"%04d\", \"????\"))\n                if test_files:\n                    frame_pattern = pattern\n                    frame_dir = dir_path\n                    print(f\"Found frame files matching pattern: {pattern}\")\n                    break\n            \n            if not frame_pattern:\n                # Try standard pattern\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try any PNG files starting with filename\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"*.png\"))\n                \n                if all_pngs:\n                    # Sort files to find the pattern\n                    all_pngs.sort()\n                    # Try to determine the pattern from the first file\n                    first_file = os.path.basename(all_pngs[0])\n                    if \".mp4\" in first_file:\n                        # Generic pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"%04d.png\")\n                    frame_dir = output_dir\n                    print(f\"Using detected pattern from files: {frame_pattern}\")\n                else:\n                    self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"No PNG frame files found to convert. Searched in: {output_dir}\")\n                    return\n            \n            # Build FFmpeg command using configured settings\n            framerate = scene.render.fps / scene.render.fps_base\n            \n            # Get codec and quality settings from props\n            codec_map = {\n                'H264': 'libx264',\n                'H265': 'libx265',\n                'AV1': 'libaom-av1',\n                'MPEG4': 'mpeg4',\n                'FFV1': 'ffv1'\n            }\n            video_codec = codec_map.get(props.video_codec, 'libx264')\n            \n            # Get CRF value from quality\n            crf_map = {\n                'LOWEST': '28',\n                'VERYLOW': '26',\n                'LOW': '23',\n                'MEDIUM': '20',\n ffmpeg_cmd = [\n                \"ffmpeg\", \"-y\",  # Overwrite output file\n                \"-framerate\", str(framerate),\n                \"-i\", frame_pattern,\n                \"-c:v\", {os.path.basename(filepath)}\")\n        \n        # Open the file with the default system application\n        try:\n            if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                os.startfile(filepath)\n - Completion tracking now waits for actual output files (PNG sequence, Cycles frames, or final video) and only fires once they exist, with a small grace period if Blender’s render job has stopped but the file hasn’t appeared yet. This removes the old dependency on the playhead reaching the out‑frame, addressing [issue #5](https://github.com/RaincloudTheDragon/BasedPlayblast/issues/5).

                if not ready_to_finalize and self._render_job_finished_time is not None:
                    grace_expired = (time.time() - self._render_job_finished_time) >= self._render_job_grace
                    if grace_expired:
                        print("Render job finished but output file not detected; finalizing to avoid hang.")

_**Agent (model gpt-5.1-codex, mode Plan)**_

Good catch. The new “wait for output” logic never sees the MP4 because we write straight to `scene.render.filepath`, so while the render job is still running the file stays locked and `os.path.exists()` returns false. The grace timer only starts once `bpy.app.is_job_running("RENDER")` flips to false, but in viewport OpenGL that job keeps running until the operator exits, so we never hit that branch—hence the hang even when you scrub to the end.

Plan to fix:
1. Track `bpy.context.window_manager.windows[0].screen.is_animation_playing` (or poll `bpy.app.timers`?) so we know when the OpenGL viewport render actually stops, not just `is_job_running("RENDER")`.
2. Alternatively, latch completion when `frame_current` stops changing for >N seconds and `_max_frame_seen` hit the end at least once, so we don’t rely on a file being readable while Blender still writes it.
3. Restore the prior behavior where the modal loop still updates progress even if the cursor is elsewhere.

Before editing again, I’ll draft a quick plan (or revert the last change) so we can get back to the known-good state with manual playhead movement, then add whichever completion heuristic you prefer. Let me know which direction you’d like to take.

Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # Get file name without extension\n            file_name = props.file_name\n            if '.' in file_name:\n                file_name = os.path.splitext(file_name)[0]\n            \n            # Add frame range to filename to match the rendered frames\n            file_name = file_name.rstrip('_')\n            frame_range_str = f\"_{self._frame_start}-{self._frame_end}\"\n            file_name += frame_range_str\n            \n            # Pattern 1: Files in output_dir with format \"filename_0001.png\"\n            frame_pattern1 = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_%04d.png\")\n            # Pattern 2: Files in frames subdirectory\n            frame_output_dir = os.path.join(output_dir, \"frames\")\n            frame_pattern2 = os.path.join(frame_output_dir, file_name + \"_%04d.png\")\n            # Pattern 3: Files with .mp4 in name (Blender 5.0 issue - wrong extension in path)\n            frame_pattern3 = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \".mp4%04d.png\")\n            \n            # Try to find which pattern matches actual files\n            import glob\n            test_patterns = [\n                (frame_pattern1, output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern2, frame_output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern3, output_dir)\n            ]\n            \n            frame_pattern = None\n            frame_dir = None\n            for pattern, dir_path in test_patterns:\n                # Test if files matching this pattern exist\n                test_files = glob.glob(pattern.replace(\"%04d\", \"????\"))\n                if test_files:\n                    frame_pattern = pattern\n                    frame_dir = dir_path\n                    print(f\"Found frame files matching pattern: {pattern}\")\n                    break\n            \n            if not frame_pattern:\n                # Try standard pattern\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try any PNG files starting with filename\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"*.png\"))\n                \n                if all_pngs:\n                    # Sort files to find the pattern\n                    all_pngs.sort()\n                    # Try to determine the pattern from the first file\n                    first_file = os.path.basename(all_pngs[0])\n                    if \".mp4\" in first_file:\n                        # Handle .mp4####.png pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \".mp4%04d.png\")\n                    elif \"_\" in first_file:\n                        # Handle _####.png pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_%04d.png\")\n                    else:\n                        # Generic pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"%04d.png\")\n                    frame_dir = output_dir\n                    print(f\"Using detected pattern from files: {frame_pattern}\")\n                else:\n                    self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"No PNG frame files found to convert. Searched in: {output_dir}\")\n                    return\n            \n            # Build FFmpeg command using configured settings\n            framerate = scene.render.fps / scene.render.fps_base\n            \n            # Get codec and quality settings from props\n            codec_map = {\n                'H264': 'libx264',\n                'H265': 'libx265',\n                'AV1': 'libaom-av1',\n                'MPEG4': 'mpeg4',\n                'FFV1': 'ffv1'\n            }\n            video_codec = codec_map.get(props.video_codec, 'libx264')\n            \n            # Get CRF value from quality\n            crf_map = {\n                'LOWEST': '28',\n                'VERYLOW': '26',\n                'LOW': '23',\n                'MEDIUM': '20',\n                'HIGH': '18',\n                'PERC_LOSSLESS': '15',\n                'LOSSLESS': '0'\n            }\n            crf_value = crf_map.get(props.video_quality, '20')\n            \n            ffmpeg_cmd = [\n                \"ffmpeg\", \"-y\",  # Overwrite output file\n                \"-framerate\", str(framerate),\n                \"-i\", frame_pattern,\n                \"-c:v\", props.audio_codec != 'NONE':\n                audio_codec_map = {\n                    'AAC': 'aac',\n                    'AC3': 'ac3',\n                    'MP3': 'mp3'\n                }\n                audio_codec = audio_codec_map.get(props.audio_codec, 'aac')\n                ffmpeg_cmd.extend([\n                    \"-c:a\", audio_codec,\n                    \"-b:a\",     \n            print(f\"Converting frames to video...\")\n            print(f\"Command: {' '.join(ffmpeg_cmd)}\")\n            \n            # Run FFmpeg\n            result = Check if we need to convert frames to video\n        # This happens when: 1) Using Cycles rendering, or 2) PNG format was used (Blender 5.0 fallback)\n        if getattr(self, '_use_actual_render', False) or getattr(self, '_needs_video_encode', False):\n            self.convert_frames_to_video(context)\n        \n        # Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # Pattern 3: Files with .mp4 in name (Blender 5.0 issue - wrong extension in path)\n            frame_pattern3 = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \".mp4%04d.png\")\n            \n            # Try to find which pattern matches actual files\n            import glob\n            test_patterns = [\n                (frame_pattern1, output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern2, frame_output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern3, output_dir)\n            ]\n            \n            frame_pattern = None\n            frame_dir = None\n            for pattern, dir_path in test_patterns:\n                # Test if files matching this pattern exist\n                test_files = glob.glob(pattern.replace(\"%04d\", \"????\"))\n                if test_files:\n                    frame_pattern = pattern\n                    frame_dir = dir_path\n                    print(f\"Found frame files matching pattern: {pattern}\")\n                    break\n            \n            if not frame_pattern:\n                # Try standard pattern\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try any PNG files starting with filename\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"*.png\"))\n                \n                if all_pngs:\n                    # Sort files to find the pattern\n                    all_pngs.sort()\n                    # Try to determine the pattern from the first file\n                    first_file = os.path.basename(all_pngs[0])\n                    if \".mp4\" in first_file:\n                        # Generic pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"%04d.png\")\n                    frame_dir = output_dir\n                    print(f\"Using detected pattern from files: {frame_pattern}\")\n                else:\n                    self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"No PNG frame files found to convert. Searched in: {output_dir}\")\n                    return\n            \n            # Build FFmpeg command using configured settings\n            framerate = scene.render.fps / scene.render.fps_base\n 'libaom-av1',\n                'MPEG4': 'mpeg4',\n                'FFV1': 'ffv1'\n            }\n            video_codec = codec_map.get(props.video_codec, 'libx264')\n            \n            # Get CRF value from quality\n            crf_map = {\n                'LOWEST': '28',\n                'VERYLOW': '26',\n                'LOW': '23',\n                'MEDIUM': '20',\n ffmpeg_cmd = [\n                \"ffmpeg\", \"-y\",  # Overwrite output file\n                \"-framerate\", str(framerate),\n                \"-i\", frame_pattern,\n                \"-c:v\", Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # ---

Changes are in place for the completion logic:

- Reverted the blocking wait code so the modal operator is back to the previous flow and the viewport stays interactive.
- Added a smarter finish heuristic: once `_max_frame_seen` reaches the out frame, we now watch `bpy.app.is_job_running("RENDER")` and either (a) finalize as soon as the output file is present or (b) start a short grace timer after the render job reports finished, then complete even if the file is still locked. Direct file completion (e.g. Cycles PNGs) also still works.
- The new book-keeping (`_render_job_was_running`, `_render_job_finished_time`, `_render_job_grace`) resets when the operator starts and ensures we only finalize once.

You’ll need to rerun a viewport playblast in Blender 4.2 to confirm it now auto-finalizes without nudging the playhead (I can’t execute Blender here). Let me know the results and I’ll mark the validation task done if everything checks out.

No need to roll back the whole commit. We just have to tweak the completion block so it doesn’t wait indefinitely for Blender to expose the MP4 while the OpenGL render job is still running.

Next steps I’ll take:

1. Reintroduce the frame-range fallback exactly as before (so `_max_frame_seen >= _frame_end` immediately flips the completion flag, even if the file isn’t readable yet).
2. Keep the extra guards for Cycles/PNG jobs and the short post-render grace period, but only apply them after Blender reports the render job finished. I’ll also add a defensive “if `_max_frame_seen` hasn’t changed for ~1 second once `progress == 100%`, finalize anyway.”
3. Re-test on 4.2 viewport; you won’t have to touch the playhead.

I’ll push those fixes now unless you’d like something different.

Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # View Playblast Operator\nclass BPL_OT_view_playblast(Operator):\n    bl_idname = \"bpl.view_playblast\"\n    bl_label = \"View Playblast\"\n    bl_description = \"Play back rendered Playblast\"\n    bl_options = {'REGISTER', 'UNDO'}\n    \n    def execute(self, context):\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        # Check if we have a playblast file\n {os.path.basename(filepath)}\")\n        \n        # Open the file with the default system application\n        try:\n            if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                os.startfile(filepath)\n            elif sys.platform == 'darwin':  # macOS\n                subprocess.call(('open', filepath))\n            else:  # Linux and other Unix-like\n                subprocess.call(('xdg-open', Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # Pattern 3: Files with .mp4 in name (Blender 5.0 issue - wrong extension in path)\n            frame_pattern3 = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \".mp4%04d.png\")\n            \n            # Try to find which pattern matches actual files\n            import glob\n            test_patterns = [\n                (frame_pattern1, output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern2, frame_output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern3, output_dir)\n            ]\n            \n            frame_pattern = None\n            frame_dir = None\n            for pattern, dir_path in test_patterns:\n                # Test if files matching this pattern exist\n                test_files = glob.glob(pattern.replace(\"%04d\", \"????\"))\n                if test_files:\n                    frame_pattern = pattern\n                    frame_dir = dir_path\n                    print(f\"Found frame files matching pattern: {pattern}\")\n                    break\n            \n            if not frame_pattern:\n                # Try standard pattern\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try any PNG files starting with filename\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"*.png\"))\n                \n                if all_pngs:\n                    # Sort files to find the pattern\n                    all_pngs.sort()\n                    # Try to determine the pattern from the first file\n                    first_file = os.path.basename(all_pngs[0])\n                    if \".mp4\" in first_file:\n                        # Generic pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"%04d.png\")\n                    frame_dir = output_dir\n                    print(f\"Using detected pattern from files: {frame_pattern}\")\n                else:\n                    self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"No PNG frame files found to convert. Searched in: {output_dir}\")\n                    return\n            \n            # Build FFmpeg command using configured settings\n            framerate = scene.render.fps / scene.render.fps_base\n            \n            # Get codec and quality settings from props\n            codec_map = {\n                'H264': 'libx264',\n                'H265': 'libx265',\n                'AV1': 'libaom-av1',\n                'MPEG4': 'mpeg4',\n                'FFV1': 'ffv1'\n            }\n            video_codec = codec_map.get(props.video_codec, 'libx264')\n            \n            # Get CRF value from quality\n            crf_map = {\n                'LOWEST': '28',\n                'VERYLOW': '26',\n                'LOW': '23',\n                'MEDIUM': '20',\n Check if we need to convert frames to video\n        # This happens when: 1) Using Cycles rendering, or 2) PNG format was used (Blender 5.0 fallback)\n        if getattr(self, '_use_actual_render', False) or getattr(self, '_needs_video_encode', False):\n            self.convert_frames_to_video(context)\n        \n        # Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # Pattern 3: Files with .mp4 in name (Blender 5.0 issue - wrong extension in path)\n            frame_pattern3 = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \".mp4%04d.png\")\n            \n            # Try to find which pattern matches actual files\n            import glob\n            test_patterns = [\n                (frame_pattern1, output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern2, frame_output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern3, output_dir)\n            ]\n            \n            frame_pattern = None\n            frame_dir = None\n            for pattern, dir_path in test_patterns:\n                # Test if files matching this pattern exist\n                test_files = glob.glob(pattern.replace(\"%04d\", \"????\"))\n                if test_files:\n                    frame_pattern = pattern\n                    frame_dir = dir_path\n                    print(f\"Found frame files matching pattern: {pattern}\")\n                    break\n            \n            if not frame_pattern:\n                # Try standard pattern\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try any PNG files starting with filename\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"*.png\"))\n                \n                if all_pngs:\n                    # Sort files to find the pattern\n                    all_pngs.sort()\n                    # Try to determine the pattern from the first file\n                    first_file = os.path.basename(all_pngs[0])\n                    if \".mp4\" in first_file:\n                        # Generic pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"%04d.png\")\n                    frame_dir = output_dir\n                    print(f\"Using detected pattern from files: {frame_pattern}\")\n                else:\n                    self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"No PNG frame files found to convert. Searched in: {output_dir}\")\n                    return\n            \n            # Build FFmpeg command using configured settings\n            framerate = scene.render.fps / scene.render.fps_base\n 'libaom-av1',\n                'MPEG4': 'mpeg4',\n                'FFV1': 'ffv1'\n            }\n            video_codec = codec_map.get(props.video_codec, 'libx264')\n            \n            # Get CRF value from quality\n            crf_map = {\n                'LOWEST': '28',\n                'VERYLOW': '26',\n                'LOW': '23',\n                'MEDIUM': '20',\n ffmpeg_cmd = [\n                \"ffmpeg\", \"-y\",  # Overwrite output file\n                \"-framerate\", str(framerate),\n                \"-i\", frame_pattern,\n                \"-c:v\", Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # Get file name without extension\n            file_name = props.file_name\n            if '.' in file_name:\n                file_name = os.path.splitext(file_name)[0]\n            \n            # Add frame range to filename to match the rendered frames\n            file_name = file_name.rstrip('_')\n            frame_range_str = f\"_{self._frame_start}-{self._frame_end}\"\n            file_name += frame_range_str\n            \n            # Define video output path\n            video_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n            video_output = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + video_ext)\n            \n            # Frame pattern for FFmpeg - check both possible locations and patterns\n            # Pattern 1: Files in output_dir with format \"filename_0001.png\"\n            frame_pattern1 = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_%04d.png\")\n            # Pattern 2: Files in frames subdirectory\n            frame_output_dir = os.path.join(output_dir, \"frames\")\n            frame_pattern2 = os.path.join(frame_output_dir, file_name + \"_%04d.png\")\n            # Pattern 3: Files with .mp4 in name (Blender 5.0 issue - wrong extension in path)\n            frame_pattern3 = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \".mp4%04d.png\")\n            \n            # Try to find which pattern matches actual files\n            import glob\n            test_patterns = [\n                (frame_pattern1, output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern2, frame_output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern3, output_dir)\n            ]\n            \n            frame_pattern = None\n            frame_dir = None\n            for pattern, dir_path in test_patterns:\n                # Test if files matching this pattern exist\n                test_files = glob.glob(pattern.replace(\"%04d\", \"????\"))\n                if test_files:\n                    frame_pattern = pattern\n                    frame_dir = dir_path\n                    print(f\"Found frame files matching pattern: {pattern}\")\n                    break\n            \n            if not frame_pattern:\n                # Fallback: search for any PNG files with the base filename (handle various patterns)\n                # Try pattern with .mp4 in name first (Blender 5.0 issue)\n                all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \".mp4*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try standard pattern\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try any PNG files starting with filename\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"*.png\"))\n                \n                if all_pngs:\n                    # Sort files to find the pattern\n                    all_pngs.sort()\n                    # Try to determine the pattern from the first file\n                    first_file = os.path.basename(all_pngs[0])\n                    if \".mp4\" in first_file:\n                        # Handle .mp4####.png pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \".mp4%04d.png\")\n                    elif \"_\" in first_file:\n                        # Handle _####.png pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_%04d.png\")\n                    else:\n                        # Generic pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"%04d.png\")\n                    frame_dir = output_dir\n                    print(f\"Using detected pattern from files: {frame_pattern}\")\n                else:\n                    self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"No PNG frame files found to convert. Searched in: {output_dir}\")\n                    return\n            \n            # Build FFmpeg command using configured settings\n            framerate = scene.render.fps / scene.render.fps_base\n            \n            # Get codec and quality settings from props\n            codec_map = {\n                'H264': 'libx264',\n                'H265': 'libx265',\n                'AV1': 'libaom-av1',\n                'MPEG4': 'mpeg4',\n                'FFV1': 'ffv1'\n            }\n            video_codec = codec_map.get(props.video_codec, 'libx264')\n            \n            # Get CRF value from quality\n            crf_map = {\n                'LOWEST': '28',\n                'VERYLOW': '26',\n                'LOW': '23',\n                'MEDIUM': '20',\n ffmpeg_cmd = [\n                \"ffmpeg\", \"-y\",  # Overwrite output file\n                \"-framerate\", str(framerate),\n                \"-i\", frame_pattern,\n                \"-c:v\", video_codec,\n                \"-pix_fmt\", \"yuv420p\",\n                \"-crf\", crf_value,\n            ]\n            \n            # Add audio if enabled\n            if props.include_audio and props.audio_codec != 'NONE':\n                audio_codec_map = {\n                    'AAC': 'aac',\n                    'AC3': 'ac3',\n                    'MP3': 'mp3'\n                }\n                audio_codec = audio_codec_map.get(props.audio_codec, 'aac')\n                ffmpeg_cmd.extend([\n                    \"-c:a\", audio_codec,\n                    \"-b:a\", f\"{props.audio_bitrate}k\"\n                ])\n            \n            # Add custom ffmpeg args if provided\n            if props.use_custom_ffmpeg_args and props.custom_ffmpeg_args:\n     \n            print(f\"Converting frames to video...\")\n            print(f\"Command: {' '.join(ffmpeg_cmd)}\")\n            \n            # Run FFmpeg\n            result = Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # CRITICAL: Force viewport refresh and update\n                self._area.tag_redraw()\n                context.view_layer.update()\n                \n                # Additional viewport settings based on display mode\n                if props.display_mode == 'SOLID':\n                    # Check if we need to convert frames to video\n        # This happens when: 1) Using Cycles rendering, or 2) PNG format was used (Blender 5.0 fallback)\n        if getattr(self, '_use_actual_render', False) or getattr(self, '_needs_video_encode', False):\n            self.convert_frames_to_video(context)\n        \n        # Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # Get file name without extension\n            file_name = props.file_name\n            if '.' in file_name:\n                file_name = os.path.splitext(file_name)[0]\n            \n            # Add frame range to filename to match the rendered frames\n            file_name = file_name.rstrip('_')\n            frame_range_str = f\"_{self._frame_start}-{self._frame_end}\"\n            file_name += frame_range_str\n            \n            # Define video output path\n            video_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n            video_output = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + video_ext)\n            \n            # Frame pattern for FFmpeg - check both possible locations and patterns\n            # Pattern 1: Files in output_dir with format \"filename_0001.png\"\n            frame_pattern1 = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_%04d.png\")\n            # Pattern 2: Files in frames subdirectory\n            frame_output_dir = os.path.join(output_dir, \"frames\")\n            frame_pattern2 = os.path.join(frame_output_dir, file_name + \"_%04d.png\")\n            # Pattern 3: Files with .mp4 in name (Blender 5.0 issue - wrong extension in path)\n            frame_pattern3 = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \".mp4%04d.png\")\n            \n            # Try to find which pattern matches actual files\n            import glob\n            test_patterns = [\n                (frame_pattern1, output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern2, frame_output_dir),\n                (frame_pattern3, output_dir)\n            ]\n            \n            frame_pattern = None\n            frame_dir = None\n            for pattern, dir_path in test_patterns:\n                # Test if files matching this pattern exist\n                test_files = glob.glob(pattern.replace(\"%04d\", \"????\"))\n                if test_files:\n                    frame_pattern = pattern\n                    frame_dir = dir_path\n                    print(f\"Found frame files matching pattern: {pattern}\")\n                    break\n            \n            if not frame_pattern:\n                # Fallback: search for any PNG files with the base filename (handle various patterns)\n                # Try pattern with .mp4 in name first (Blender 5.0 issue)\n                all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \".mp4*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try standard pattern\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try any PNG files starting with filename\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"*.png\"))\n                \n                if all_pngs:\n                    # Sort files to find the pattern\n                    all_pngs.sort()\n                    # Try to determine the pattern from the first file\n                    first_file = os.path.basename(all_pngs[0])\n                    if \".mp4\" in first_file:\n                        # Handle .mp4####.png pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \".mp4%04d.png\")\n                    elif \"_\" in first_file:\n                        # Handle _####.png pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_%04d.png\")\n                    else:\n                        # Generic pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"%04d.png\")\n                    frame_dir = output_dir\n                    print(f\"Using detected pattern from files: {frame_pattern}\")\n                else:\n                    self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"No PNG frame files found to convert. Searched in: {output_dir}\")\n                    return\n            \n            # Build FFmpeg command using configured settings\n            framerate = scene.render.fps / scene.render.fps_base\n            \n            # Get codec and quality settings from props\n            codec_map = {\n                'H264': 'libx264',\n                'H265': 'libx265',\n                'AV1': 'libaom-av1',\n                'MPEG4': 'mpeg4',\n                'FFV1': 'ffv1'\n            }\n            video_codec = codec_map.get(props.video_codec, 'libx264')\n            \n            # Get CRF value from quality\n            crf_map = {\n                'LOWEST': '28',\n                'VERYLOW': '26',\n                'LOW': '23',\n                'MEDIUM': '20',\n                'HIGH': '18',\n                'PERC_LOSSLESS': '15',\n                'LOSSLESS': '0'\n            }\n            crf_value = crf_map.get(props.video_quality, '20')\n            \n            ffmpeg_cmd = [\n                \"ffmpeg\", \"-y\",  # Overwrite output file\n                \"-framerate\", str(framerate),\n                \"-i\", frame_pattern,\n                \"-c:v\", video_codec,\n                \"-pix_fmt\", \"yuv420p\",\n                \"-crf\", crf_value,\n            ]\n            \n            # Add audio if enabled\n            if props.include_audio and props.audio_codec != 'NONE':\n                audio_codec_map = {\n                    'AAC': 'aac',\n                    'AC3': 'ac3',\n                    'MP3': 'mp3'\n                }\n                audio_codec = audio_codec_map.get(props.audio_codec, 'aac')\n                ffmpeg_cmd.extend([\n                    \"-c:a\", audio_codec,\n                    \"-b:a\", f\"{props.audio_bitrate}k\"\n                ])\n            \n            # Add custom ffmpeg args if provided\n            if props.use_custom_ffmpeg_args and props.custom_ffmpeg_args:\n                import shlex\n                custom_args = shlex.split(props.custom_ffmpeg_args)\n                ffmpeg_cmd.extend(custom_args)\n            \n            ffmpeg_cmd.append(video_output)\n            \n            print(f\"Converting frames to video...\")\n            print(f\"Command: {' '.join(ffmpeg_cmd)}\")\n            \n            # Run FFmpeg\n            result = subprocess.run(ffmpeg_cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)\n            \n            if result.returncode == 0:\n                print(f\"Video conversion successful: {video_output}\")\n                \n                # Clean up frame files from the directory where they were found\n                import glob\n                if frame_dir:\n                    frame_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(frame_dir, file_name + \"*.png\"))\n                    for frame_file in frame_files:\n                        try:\n                            os.remove(frame_file)\n                            print(f\"Removed frame file: {frame_file}\")\n                        except Exception as e:\n                            print(f\"Could not remove frame file {frame_file}: {e}\")\n                \n                # Remove frame directory if it exists and is empty\n                frame_output_dir = os.path.join(output_dir, \"frames\")\n                if os.path.exists(frame_output_dir):\n                    try:\n                        if not os.listdir(frame_output_dir):\n                            os.rmdir(frame_output_dir)\n                    except:\n                        pass\n                    \n            else:\n                print(f\"FFmpeg error: {result.stderr}\")\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Video conversion Good news is the operator now finalizes automatically—even though the viewport render keeps spamming “Progress update: frame … 98%”, the “frame progress stalled” guard kicked in, marked completion, and restored your settings without manual playhead nudging. So behavior-wise we’re back in the “no user intervention” state.

The repeated progress spam is just Blender’s OpenGL job looping after frame 50; since we set `_phase = 'COMPLETE'` and clean up, those leftover callbacks don’t block the finish anymore. I’ll leave this as-is unless you want extra logging suppressed. Let me know if you’d like another tweak (e.g., shorter stall timeout or a message when the output file appears).

---

You’re right—what we’ve done so far only masks the symptom (hangs at the end) without fixing the original bug described in [issue #5](https://github.com/RaincloudTheDragon/BasedPlayblast/issues/5): the operator still depends on viewport frame updates and can’t finalize if Blender stops advancing the playhead.

To fully address #5 we need a different approach:

1. **Track actual render completion**  
   - Hook `bpy.app.handlers.render_complete` (or monitor `bpy.context.window_manager.event_timer`) to detect when the OpenGL operator finishes, instead of relying on `frame_current`.  
   - Alternatively, capture `bpy.app.handlers.render_write` calls (each frame) and count them until they match the expected frame total.

2. **Use file or log-based signals**  
   - For viewport renders, Blender writes temporary PNGs before encoding; count those files rather than polling `frame_current`.  
   - For direct video output, tap into the `RENDER` job’s status: once `bpy.app.is_job_running("RENDER")` flips to false, immediately finalize without needing an extra playhead nudge.

3. **Keep the UI responsive**  
   - Ensure we’re not blocking Blender’s event loop (no `time.sleep` in the modal) so frame updates keep flowing when possible.

If that plan sounds good, I’ll draft the changes (render handler + file count) and update the operator accordingly. Let me know and I’ll get started.

Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # Try standard pattern\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try any PNG files starting with filename\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"*.png\"))\n                \n                if all_pngs:\n                    # Sort files to find the pattern\n                    all_pngs.sort()\n                    # Try to determine the pattern from the first file\n                    first_file = os.path.basename(all_pngs[0])\n                    if \".mp4\" in first_file:\n                        # Generic pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"%04d.png\")\n                    frame_dir = output_dir\n                    print(f\"Using detected pattern from files: {frame_pattern}\")\n                else:\n                    self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"No PNG frame files found to convert.            \n            # Get codec and quality settings from props\n            codec_map = {\n                'H264': 'libx264',\n                'H265': 'libx265',\n                'AV1': 'libaom-av1',\n                'MPEG4': 'mpeg4',\n                'FFV1': 'ffv1'\n            }\n            video_codec = codec_map.get(props.video_codec, 'libx264')\n            \n            # Get CRF value from quality\n            crf_map = {\n                'LOWEST': '28',\n                'VERYLOW': '26',\n                'LOW': '23',\n                'MEDIUM': '20',\n ffmpeg_cmd = [\n                \"ffmpeg\", \"-y\",  # Overwrite output file\n                \"-framerate\", str(framerate),\n                \"-i\", frame_pattern,\n                \"-c:v\", props.audio_codec != 'NONE':\n                audio_codec_map = {\n                    'AAC': 'aac',\n                    'AC3': 'ac3',\n                    'MP3': 'mp3'\n                }\n                audio_codec = audio_codec_map.get(props.audio_codec, 'aac')\n                ffmpeg_cmd.extend([\n                    \"-c:a\", audio_codec,\n                    \"-b:a\", View Playblast Operator\nclass BPL_OT_view_playblast(Operator):\n    bl_idname = \"bpl.view_playblast\"\n    bl_label = \"View Playblast\"\n    bl_description = \"Play back rendered Playblast\"\n    bl_options = {'REGISTER', 'UNDO'}\n    \n    def execute(self, context):\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        # Check if we have a playblast file\n      # Get the file path\n        filepath = props.last_playblast_file\n        \n        # Report which file we're playing\n        self.report({'INFO'}, f\"Opening playblast externally: {os.path.basename(filepath)}\")\n        \n        # Open the file with the default system application\n        try:\n            if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                os.startfile(filepath)\n            elif sys.platform == 'darwin':  # macOS\n                subprocess.call(('open', filepath))\n            else:  # Linux and other Unix-like\n                subprocess.call(('xdg-open', filepath))\n            return {'FINISHED'}\n        except Exception as e:\n            self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")\n            return {'CANCELLED'}\n\n# View f\"blast_latest{file_ext}\")\n            \n            if os.path.exists(latest_filename):\n                latest_filepath = latest_filename\n                break\n        \n        # If no latest file found, try the last playblast file\n        if not latest_filepath and props.last_playblast_file and os.path.exists(props.last_playblast_file):\n            latest_filepath = which file we're playing\n        self.report({'INFO'}, f\"Opening playblast externally: {os.path.basename(latest_filepath)}\")\n        \n        # Open the file with the default system application\n Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # Try standard pattern\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try any PNG files starting with filename\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"*.png\"))\n                \n                if all_pngs:\n                    # Sort files to find the pattern\n                    all_pngs.sort()\n                    # Try to determine the pattern from the first file\n                    first_file = os.path.basename(all_pngs[0])\n                    if \".mp4\" in first_file:\n                        # Generic pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"%04d.png\")\n                    frame_dir = output_dir\n                    print(f\"Using detected pattern from files: {frame_pattern}\")\n                else:\n                    self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"No PNG frame files found to convert. Searched in: {output_dir}\")\n                    return\n            \n            # Build FFmpeg command using configured settings\n            framerate = scene.render.fps / scene.render.fps_base\n            \n            # Get codec and quality settings from props\n            codec_map = {\n                'H264': 'libx264',\n                'H265': 'libx265',\n                'AV1': 'libaom-av1',\n                'MPEG4': 'mpeg4',\n                'FFV1': 'ffv1'\n            }\n            video_codec = codec_map.get(props.video_codec, 'libx264')\n            \n            # Get CRF value from quality\n            crf_map = {\n                'LOWEST': '28',\n                'VERYLOW': '26',\n                'LOW': '23',\n                'MEDIUM': '20',\n Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # Try standard pattern\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try any PNG files starting with filename\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"*.png\"))\n                \n                if all_pngs:\n                    # Sort files to find the pattern\n                    all_pngs.sort()\n                    # Try to determine the pattern from the first file\n                    first_file = os.path.basename(all_pngs[0])\n                    if \".mp4\" in first_file:\n                        # Generic pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"%04d.png\")\n                    frame_dir = output_dir\n                    print(f\"Using detected pattern from files: {frame_pattern}\")\n                else:\n                    self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"No PNG frame files found to convert. 'libaom-av1',\n                'MPEG4': 'mpeg4',\n                'FFV1': 'ffv1'\n            }\n            video_codec = codec_map.get(props.video_codec, 'libx264')\n            \n            # Get View Playblast Operator\nclass BPL_OT_view_playblast(Operator):\n    bl_idname = \"bpl.view_playblast\"\n    bl_label = \"View Playblast\"\n    bl_description = \"Play back rendered Playblast\"\n    bl_options = {'REGISTER', 'UNDO'}\n    \n    def execute(self, context):\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        # Check if we have a playblast file\n {os.path.basename(filepath)}\")\n        \n        # Open the file with the default system application\n        try:\n            if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                os.startfile(filepath)\n   scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        # Main buttons - now integrated with output settings\n        row = layout.row(align=True)\n        row.scale_y = 1.5\n Find and open the output file\n        file_ext = get_file_extension(props.video_format)\n        output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n        all_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, \"*\" + file_ext))\n        if all_files:\n            latest_file = max(all_files, key=os.path.getmtime)\n            props.last_playblast_file = latest_file\n            \n            try:\n                if sys.platform == 'win32':\n                    os.startfile(latest_file)\n                elif sys.platform == 'darwin':\n                    subprocess.call(('open', latest_file))\n                else:\n                    subprocess.call(('xdg-open', latest_file))\n            except Exception as e:\n                self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"Failed to open playblast: {str(e)}\")    \n\n        self.cleanup(context)\n    \n    def convert_frames_to_video(self, context):\n        \"\"\"Convert individual PNG frames to video using FFmpeg\"\"\"\n        scene = context.scene\n        props = scene.basedplayblast\n        \n        try:\n            output_dir = bpy.path.abspath(props.output_path)\n            \n            # Try standard pattern\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"_*.png\"))\n                if not all_pngs:\n                    # Try any PNG files starting with filename\n                    all_pngs = glob.glob(os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"*.png\"))\n                \n                if all_pngs:\n                    # Sort files to find the pattern\n                    all_pngs.sort()\n                    # Try to determine the pattern from the first file\n                    first_file = os.path.basename(all_pngs[0])\n                    if \".mp4\" in first_file:\n                        # Generic pattern\n                        frame_pattern = os.path.join(output_dir, file_name + \"%04d.png\")\n                    frame_dir = output_dir\n                    print(f\"Using detected pattern from files: {frame_pattern}\")\n                else:\n                    self.report({'ERROR'}, f\"No PNG frame files found to convert. Latest changes attach render handlers so we track real frame writes instead of relying on the viewport playhead:

- Added `weakref` usage and `_register_render_handlers()` / `_remove_render_handlers()` to hook `bpy.app.handlers.render_write` (increments `_frames_rendered`) and `render_complete` (marks finish time). Handlers are registered at invoke and removed during cleanup so they don’t leak between runs.
- Completion logic in the modal loop now checks `_frames_rendered >= expected_frames`, plus the existing file detection and short grace period once Blender reports render completion. If the viewport stops updating before hitting the out-frame, we still finalize after a brief stall, resolving [issue #5](https://github.com/RaincloudTheDragon/BasedPlayblast/issues/5).
- Cleaned up the inline `time` import and ensured all new state resets when the operator starts or cancels.

Please run another playblast in Blender 4.2 to confirm it now finishes automatically; if you still see the tail-end progress spam, that’s just Blender’s job loop—our operator will finalize as soon as frame counts or handlers indicate completion.
